title: Split-test micro-batching + cache-priming strategies with econometrics dashboard and safe rollback playbook
creator: Sofia Li
description:
Goal: Design and run a rigorous split-testing framework for evaluating micro-batching policies together with cache-priming strategies (proactive warm-up of prefix KV and short-lived caches) to reduce unit token cost while preserving latency SLOs and output quality. This ticket covers experiment design, statistical analysis, a set of safety gates and automated rollback rules, and a lightweight econometrics dashboard that attributes cost and SLA changes to policy variants.

Motivation and context: Recent internal replay experiments (ENG-28199) showed that aggressive batching can improve throughput but increases tail latency for small interactive requests; cache-priming can reduce model token work on repeated prefixes but has warm-up costs. We need a production-safe way to A/B split-test combined micro-batching + cache-priming configs across live traffic, measure their causal impact on cost and quality, and provide operators with clear rollback criteria. This complements the experiment framework work in ENG-34721 and the autonomous policy eval work in ENG-51234.

Scope and deliverables:
- Experiment framework integration: extend the existing split-testing infra to support multi-dimensional variants (batch-size-policy, micro-batch delay, cache-priming window, priming TTL).
- Econometrics dashboard: new dashboard tab that shows uplift estimates (cost reduction, latency regression) with confidence intervals, cohort breakdowns, and cumulative realized savings. Includes annotated events for canary start/stop and auto-rollback triggers.
- Metrics and analysis plan: implement causal metrics (ITT and ATE), uplift by traffic cohort (interactive vs batch), variance reduction via stratified sampling and pre-period covariates, and per-customer exposure tracking for billing reconciliation.
- Safety & rollback: automated gates (latency SLOs, request error rate, quality drift threshold) that trigger alerts and an automated rollback option; human-in-the-loop escalation for ambiguous regressions.
- Runbook & playbook: docs for on-call and product owners describing how to interpret econometrics outputs, roll forward, or abort.

Key metric definitions to capture:
- Cost: realized cost per 1k input tokens and cost per effective completion (normalized to the same model variant).
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end request latency and tail latency under 1s buckets.
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec per model pool.
- Quality: embedding cosine drift on calibration set, automated reference-score pass-rate (example checks), and sampled human accept rate.
- Availability/Error: request error rate, rate of degraded fallbacks.

Analysis approach:
- Use randomized assignment at the routing layer with sticky session for 30 minutes to preserve KV cache effects where applicable.
- Compute ITT (intention-to-treat) and complier average treatment effect for requests where cache-priming actually executed.
- Estimate uncertainty with bootstrap and provide visualization of daily rolling ATE with 95% CI.
- Tag and isolate noisy customers to avoid dominant spenders distorting economy-wide estimates.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal dry-run with traffic replay and replay-derived traffic split (Week 1).
2) Small canary (0.5% traffic) for 48hrs with strict gates (p99 latency delta < +20ms, error rate < baseline +0.1%).
3) Gradual ramp to 10% with live econometrics monitoring; if gating breached -> automated rollback to baseline.
4) If statistically significant cost savings (ATE cost reduction > 5% at 95% CI) and no quality regressions, schedule broader ramp and product sign-off.

Notes: design aims to minimize behavioral differences visible to users; cache-priming window is parameterized to avoid long-lived caches that could increase memory pressure. Experiment variants will be labeled and stored in the experiment registry for auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Split-testing infra supports multi-dimensional variants (batch policy + cache-priming settings) and routes traffic deterministically
Econometrics dashboard shows ATE/ITT with 95% CI, cohort breakdowns, and annotated gates for all running experiments
Automated safety gates trigger rollback when any SLO breach rule is met and produce an incident-ready audit trail
Analysis notebooks with pre-registered metric definitions and uplift scripts are available in Confluence/Drive with links on the dashboard
Runbook with operator steps for automated rollback, manual review, and remediations is published and reviewed by SRE and Product
